resp is stored as answered (1 to 5), not reverse-scored. Items spa_1, spa_3, spa_7, spa_11, spa_13 and spa_14 are reverse-keyed; score them as 6 - resp before summing. The study's supplement (s002.docx) gives this keying, and it reproduces the published mean (43.21), SD (10.52) and alpha (0.877). Summing the raw values gives SD 9.00 and alpha 0.805.

resp is the raw true/false answer (0/1), not the scored SAD. To reproduce the published SAD total (mean 13.68, SD 7.47, r = 0.195 with expressive suppression), score sad_2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 24 and 26 as 1 - resp and sum all 28. Pooled from MECO L1's two collection rounds, which are different people at mostly different sites: cov_sample 1 = wave 1 (13 sites), 2 = wave 2 (16 sites). It is not a panel, so the round is cov_sample rather than wave. cov_language is the language and cov_site the release's site code. The 42 wave-1 Norwegian readers answered 47 questions (text 6 question 4 was not administered).

Item codes are shared only where the question is the same. Only texts 1, 3, 7, 11 and 12 are translations of a common original (the authors' is.matched flag); their questions are text{t}_q{q} across sites. The other 7 texts were written per language, so their items carry a language or text-version prefix (e.g. du_text2_q1) and are answered only by that site's readers: the table is sparse by design, with a median of 45 readers per item. A version is shared across sites or rounds only where the text is identical (no and tr across rounds, en with en_uk, the two Hindi sites except text 5, German wave 2 as ge_v2, sp with sp_ch on texts 2, 4, 5 and 9). Eight wave-1 matched questions that are a different question in that language get site-specific codes (ee_text3_q1, ee_text3_q2, sp_text3_q3, he_text1_q3, he_text12_q4, ru_text12_q4, gr_text12_q2, tr_text12_q3).

Wave 2 published no comprehension-question wording, so for wave-2 sites the equivalence of the matched questions (text{t}_q{q}) is assumed from the authors' design and is unverified. Two wave-2 sites contradict it in their responses and are coded site-specific instead: ru_mo for all 48 items (its per-question accuracy does not match any other site, nor wave-1 Russian on identical texts) and ba for text 11.

Three studies of the same paired-choice task, pooled; cov_sample names the study. LargeValence_2017 and LargeValence_2018 share 7 pictures (Cat, Crow, Doctor, Fire, Frustrated, Lake, War); LowValence_2017 uses 7 others (Flowers, Food, Grass, House, Monkey, Sunset, Timber). No one saw both sets, so the two halves share no items. Each trial is two rows: resp 1 for the picture chosen, 0 for the one passed over; trial numbers restart within each study.

The CASEN time-use follow-ups (u1_a to u11_a, u15_a to u17_a: minutes per day spent on each activity, 0 to 1440) are not included. They are measured quantities, not item responses. The yes/no and rating items they follow (u1 to u22) are all here.

Item codes are the survey's. b1a-b4: ASER tool, adaptive (b1c, b2, b3, b4 are asked only on certain earlier outcomes, so they have few rows; b4 has 2). c = written abstract, d = oral abstract, e = oral anchored (word problem); the digit is the operation (1 add, 2 subtract, 3 multiply, 4 divide) and _v1-_v4 the survey version. Each child got one version, and versions use different numbers, so c1_v1 and c1_v2 are different items. f1 = oral anchored market problem; f2 = pretend market, scored as the authors do (a total within rounding of the exact one counts). Division answers within a rounding band count as correct, per the enumerators' coding. The randomised-hint follow-up to f1 is not included.

Study 3a wave 1 only, first attempts only. Each child solved one of two variants of each subtraction and division problem (randomised); the item code names the operands. The mystery-shopping and hypothetical-market questions are not included (each uses the child's own goods and prices, so no two children answer the same item), nor are second attempts and post-hint attempts (asked only after a wrong answer or under a randomised hint). Study 3a wave 2 is a different instrument and is not here. cov_market is the authors' corrected market id.

resp scores the annotator's choice against the CIFAR-10 ground-truth label (itemcov_true_category), which is itself a label assigned when the dataset was built and is wrong for some images; Peterson et al. (2019) use the human label distribution, not the key, as the target. The chosen class is in resp_raw (core) and text (cifar10h_nom).

text is not an option the student chose: it is the graders' classification of the free-text answer (in answer_text) into one of five accuracy categories, converted from finer facet-level annotations and hand-revised by the task organisers. resp collapses it to SemEval's 2-way scheme (1 = correct, 0 = any other label). id is module_student: student numbers restart in each module, and each module was given to a different group of children.

Forfeited games: winner follows Retrosheet's forfeit code, not the score (forfeit V = agent_b, H = agent_a; T, ruled a no-decision, = draw). homefield is always agent_a, the team Retrosheet lists as home; neutral-site games (Tokyo, London, Mexico City series, etc.) are not marked, and park identifies them. league NAssn is Retrosheet's NA (National Association, 1871-75), renamed so it is not read as missing.

agent_a is always the winning team (the source records only winner and loser, not side or serve), so winner is always agent_a; do not read an agent_a advantage into it. Agents are doubles teams keyed by their two pklmart player ids. Data are player-entered, mostly amateur games, and sparse: most teams appear in one game.

excluded = 1 marks the decisions of judges whose median time per judgement was under 5 seconds (484 of 3,969). Sangwin & Kinnear dropped these as nonserious judges, and their analyses and the Kinnear et al. CJ meta-analysis use the remaining 3,485.

Raters who were not logged in to Zooniverse (rater_logged_in = 0, 67,558 decisions) are identified per browser session, so one person may appear as several raters. The two sessions show the same 1,111 images, the second after brightness equalisation; analyse them separately or model session.

No game ends in a draw. Under SSCAIT's rules a crashing bot loses (crashed names it, 3,538 games), and a game that hits the time limit (90 in-game minutes, or 5 minutes with no unit dying) goes to the bot with the higher kills+razings score (timelimit = 1, 1,437 games; the API notes these as "draw;"). Filter on both if only games played to destruction are wanted.

Wikipedia prints each score without saying whose comes first, so score_a/score_b give the higher score to the listed winner. Matches before about 1890 were decided on goals: 58 have no points score (score_a/score_b blank, printed score in score_raw), and the early points values are as the pages give them. Home side is the venue's country (Belfast counts as Ireland); World Cup and other third-country matches have homefield blank. Only matches both sides capped are included: the 1920-28 Australia (New South Wales) v New Zealand and South Africa matches and uncapped touring XVs are excluded.

resp runs in the opposite direction to the source's SPSS file and paper: here 1 = 'No! Totally disagree!' through 5 = 'Yes! Totally agree!', whereas the deposit codes 1 = 'Yes! Totally agree!' through 5 = 'No! Totally disagree!' on all eleven items. IRW numbers the response labels from least to most agreement, as for this study's other scales. To join resp back to the deposit or read it with the deposit's codebook, use 6 - resp.

The reason_less_rigorous_* (9) and reason_no_deception_* (8) items are not answered by respondents: they are themes the study's authors coded from two open-ended answers ("Do you think that studies that use deception are inherently less rigorous...? Please elaborate" and "Why don't you use deception in your experimental designs?"), as deposited. 1 = the answer was coded with that theme, 0 = it was coded with others; one answer can carry several themes. Respondents who left the question blank have no rows.
